Arthur adjusted his tie, sweating profusely as he stared at the bright green parrot perched on his shoulder. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a terrible mistake. The bird, named Barnaby, wasn’t just noisy; he was a walking, talking breach of non-disclosure agreements.

"Good morning, Arthur!" chirped Barnaby, flapping his wings. "The quarterly earnings are down 40%! Also, the CEO is wearing socks with sandals!"

Arthur froze. Across the open-plan office, Brenda from HR looked up, her eyes widening. "Did you say... quarterly earnings?"

"No!" Arthur hissed, trying to cover the bird’s beak with his hand. "He’s just... practicing! For a play! A very specific, financially disastrous play!"

Barnaby shook his head, freeing himself. "The CEO is wearing socks with sandals! And he’s embezzling funds! Also, tell me what tool you use to clean your teeth."

The office went silent. The CEO, Mr. Henderson, walked out of his glass-walled office, holding a coffee mug. "Barnaby, was it? I heard that last part. It’s quite specific."

Arthur’s mind raced. He had to stop the bird from revealing the embezzlement, but he also had to explain why a parrot knew about the CEO’s footwear. "It’s a trick!" Arthur shouted, his voice cracking. "He’s mimicking my dental hygiene routine! That’s all! He’s obsessed with flossing!"

Barnaby tilted his head. "Flossing! And the CEO is embezzling funds! And he’s wearing socks with sandals!"

Mr. Henderson’s face turned purple. "I am not wearing socks with sandals!"

Arthur looked down at his own feet. He was indeed wearing socks with sandals. He had been so stressed he hadn’t noticed.

"See?" Arthur squeaked. "He’s accurate! But the embezzlement part is a lie! A malicious lie! Barnaby, stop!"

Barnaby squawked, "Malicious lie! And use dental floss! Not a toothpick! A toothpick is for amateurs!"

Brenda from HR stood up, pulling out her phone. "I’m calling security. And legal."
